original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Independently audit PR #3818's partial union-support completion prune against the full unpruned canonical restored-word domain at n=4, L=8, and compare the current engine's union-only hit set.
scope_change_reason: Live #1166 handoff #19026415 and open PR #3818 add a new union-support prune after #2973's parity correction; merged #3005 already independently replays the corrected L18/L20 result. This pass narrows to the exact new partial-prefix implication instead of repeating the old-prune audit or expanding to L22.
bottleneck_link: An unsound prefix rejection can remove a universal completion and invalidate a finite census exclusion; this audit checks that boundary on a complete small domain.
stop_rule: Exhaust all 4^8 label words without union pruning, retain every canonical restored completion, and stop after verifying that no universal completion lies below any prefix rejected by the proposed bound; stop earlier if a counterexample is found.
evidence: PASS_F7_L22_UNION_PRUNE_TINY_EXHAUSTIVE: all 65,536 raw words scanned; 105 canonical restored words and 26 universal words; all 26 survive the union rule; 840 prefix/completion checks; zero rejected prefixes have a universal completion. The exact PR #3818 C source at head e09a08b5f85e648be373bece1b6ea1265d5ea8fa also returns the same 22-word hit set for split (4,4) in union-only mode.
author: homelab-12 research pass, with OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance (GPT-6 Luna xhigh) was used for source tracing, the independent verifier, analysis, and writing. No formal proof assistant or independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can the PR #3818 length-22 (9,9) exclusion be independently replayed with a separate engine?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The tiny-domain audit does not validate the billion-node L22 split search; independent complete evidence would address the next open census obligation.
open_questions.first_step: Adapt the independent PR #3005 engine's domain guard and receipts for n=7, L=22, split (9,9), with a named node cap and resource budget.
open_questions.blocked_by: The PR #3818 run records 388,563,293 nodes; the donor excluded a full seven-label replay from this pass without a separate compute decision.
